look_here_first: LOOK FIRST at mature spikelets and the culm base: spikelets usually FLATTENED with relatively long DECIDUOUS floral scales, typically 3.2–4.5 mm, and a cormlike thickened culm base. Contrast odoratus mature corky rachilla that breaks into one-fruited units.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Perennial flatsedge of wet or disturbed soils, with leaflike bracts radiating beneath the flower cluster.

key_traits.label: Base
key_traits.text: Cormlike swollen basal region is supporting character; photograph excavated plant without losing the base.

key_traits.label: Inflorescence
key_traits.text: Terminal compound umbrella-like cluster with rays and leaflike bracts, relatively straw-colored radiating flattened spikelets.

key_traits.label: Spikelets
key_traits.text: Flattened, floral scales commonly 3.2–4.5(–6) mm and DECIDUOUS; mature fruits and exposed rachilla needed to distinguish odoratus.

key_traits.label: Fruit
key_traits.text: One achene under each fertile scale. Three stigma branches can help support the key, but use entire mature specimen.
